# Patrick Mockridge

> Independent protocol engineer working on privacy protocols, consensus systems, formal verification, and numerical provenance. The method is to specify the failure mode before the architecture, prove what can be proved, contain what cannot, and record provenance with every result.

- [CV (PDF)](https://patrickmockridge.github.io/cv.pdf): one-page PDF.

- [fitba](https://patrickmockridge.github.io/fitba/): Aberdeen FC data-centric fan site.
- [Contact](mailto:patrickmockridge@gmail.com): protocol review, rescue, verification, advisory.

## Selected work

- [DarkWow](https://patrickmockridge.github.io/darkwow/): a private bearer-note system: the note is the asset, possession is authority, and no protocol-level administrator can freeze or confiscate it. The fork-original contract set includes ZK Box and Purse, a ZK-based Identity/Oracle/Attestation/Stablecoin suite, an object-capability bridge, and a no-freeze Promissory Note (the issuer is the note's counterparty for redemption; credential issuers and relayers are explicit counterparties). Object-capability governance, Uncle Merkle consensus, a per-block Pedersen mass balance over native-token calls, and a Lean 4 proof-status ledger. The fork's Lean 4 gadget-level proofs cover `less_than_or_equal`, `base_div`, and `is_not_equal`; the current contracts use `less_than_or_equal` and a quotient-remainder pattern. Research prototype; mainnet TBD; no third-party audit; Lean-modelled opcodes and gadgets are partial; the gate checks instance derivation for 167 contract circuits (179 walked); it does not prove circuit correctness; six assumptions remain; OBL-Z12 is closed for the known quotient circuits in the obligation register while the proof-status ledger still marks the general range-check discharge as partly open, and one validator defect (OBL-C279) is deferred to the next release. The bridge refuses every deposit by default; with `bridge-verify` on, Monero DLEq and Litecoin Merkle proofs are implemented (Litecoin MWEB range proofs deferred), while Ethereum, Zcash, and Aztec remain fail-closed or stubbed.
- [Rholo](https://patrickmockridge.github.io/rholo/): a Rust node for the rho-calculus, ported from the preserved Scala reference of the former RChain node (twelve crates), plus original Rust OCapN interop and the qucalc governance crate. RChain comes out of Greg Meredith's pre-Bitcoin enterprise lineage: he was Principal Architect of Microsoft's BizTalk process orchestration and of an ATM network management solution for AT&T/NCR. The design target is multi-tenant SaaS — many concurrent tenants, narrow delegated authority, and long-running inter-organisational workflows — rather than a single-ledger DeFi shape; sharding is untested at scale. Native object capabilities, horizontal scale-out by design, and a law register tied to the node by conformance corpora. Pre-release; tagged testnet release v0.1.0 with a public community testnet; 91 laws across 131 entries, 122 proved (36 tied to the node by conformance corpora); October 2026 re-audit: no P0, 3 P1, 3 P2, 2 P3/assurance (C345–C352 addressed, C348 residual); no external audit firm.
- [R-Cash](https://patrickmockridge.github.io/r-cash/): a permissionless multi-currency account and cross-border payments network on Rholo — the on-chain payments core of a Wise-shaped product. Hold, receive, convert, pay, get paid; liquidity providers earn the FX spread across a mesh of direct pairs, with no router and no mandatory USD hop. Per-currency issuer clusters, FxPool and LiquidityLock per market, an oracle hub, and a TransferBook with claim, expiry, refund, and one terminal state. v0.5 devnet-only prototype; no fiat custody, no real value, no external audit, no mainnet; Rholo is pre-testnet; do not use with real funds. 13/13 behavioural suites plus CLI demo passed on a fixed-node devnet (27 October 2026); 929-line specification; Lean 4 project rholphin and five TLA+ models; verification is traceability plus tests, not extraction.
- [R-Gen](https://patrickmockridge.github.io/r-gen/): Rholang contracts and Lean 4 proofs for Dan Robles' CoEngineers and Ingenesist vision. Engineering work becomes a claim, validation is its quality, and the pair is a K-Asset that keeps its qualifications, adjudication, and provenance. Seven core deploy terms, 16 components and 10 state cells; ten behavioural suites with 291 assertions on a fresh devnet (4 November 2026); 36 Lean files and 131 public theorems audited; 32-pair race matrix. Devnet-only, unaudited, no real value; extensions (receipts, payments, risk, panels, governance, metrics, client) are not implemented; Lean proves the model, not a mechanized Rholang refinement; the arm map is hand-transcribed; the seven papers are third-party copyright, not AGPL.
- [R-Share](https://patrickmockridge.github.io/r-share/): on-chain booking and rental primitives for Rholo, settled through R-Cash. A listing owns units, a unit owns slots, and a booking holds capacity over an interval with escrow, cancellation, deposits, disputes and tickets. Thirteen deploy terms; 16/16 behavioural suites on a fresh devnet (3 November 2026, rholo e2d073d, r-cash 49b441d); 20/30 coverage cells; seven settlement scenarios; Lean allocator proved-model (acquire_no_double_owner). Devnet-only, unaudited, pinned to R-Cash v0.5, no real value; per-listing serialization is the accepted hotspot; no privacy; no KYC or legal identity; providerDeliveryBreach and partialPerformance remain design; the 37 axiom audits are an internal Lean check, not a security audit.
- [Azoth](https://patrickmockridge.github.io/azoth/): chemical-engineering calculations in Python and Rust, written twice by hand from one TOML declaration, where every result carries its provenance and unsupported answers are refused. v0.1.1; not on PyPI; not for design work yet.
- [Mudra](https://patrickmockridge.github.io/mudra/): a proof-of-trace system for spreadsheets and small programs. A constant-size Halo2 proof binds a program digest, input/output hashes, return value, and step count. It does not constrain each instruction; per-instruction correctness relies on deterministic replay with the witness. Research build.

## Research

- [Research and writing](https://patrickmockridge.github.io/research/): the Romeo-Juliet critical risk-analysis framework for coordinated systems under information asymmetry — AI, blockchains, politics, business, engineering; UNISS/Ingenesist simulations of influence, secrecy, and layered compromise; an NFL Big Data Bowl entry on the Combine pressure signal and playing-time allocation gap, with a free-agent valuation of the role premium; the Ingenesist archive.
- [NFL Big Data Bowl 2027](https://github.com/PatrickMockridge/nfl-big-data-bowl-2027): a judged entry showing that a 10 Hz Combine burst predicts interior pressure (+0.354 SD per SD) where the 40-yard dash and 10-yard split do not; it also shows a sack association (+0.317), though the stopwatch is the stronger out-of-sample sack model and the outcome sits below the reliability gate. The cap pays for performance (+0.328 log points per SD) while playing time follows prior snaps and draft capital. A follow-on free-agent valuation puts the median team's uncut role premium at about $7.05M a year — $2.82M gross / $1.82M net at a 0.40 capture assumption after a $1M implementation cost, and −$0.45M net for the conservative EDGE/safety/corner case; the +0.179 log-point premium on 2026 APY falls to +0.049 with contract-structure controls (n=253). The preregistered RJF/Yellow Square test is a wide null reported as fallback evidence.
- [Ingenesist archive](https://app.ardrive.io/#/drives/57a3e07f-7adb-4bcf-b013-154869c56e33?name=Ingenesist+Project): Dan Roble's presentations and papers.
